newsitem.title: UK: Dated Brent trades at weaker July Brent -30 cts.
newsitem.headline: Dated Brent trades at weaker July Brent -30 cts.

text.p: Dated Brent traded at a weaker July Brent -30 cents on Friday, traders said.
The cargo, due to load June 12-14, was sold by one European major to another and follows a deal for a June 8-10 cargo on Thursday at July Brent -24 cents.
Two other Brents also changed hands on Friday, a June 8-10 loader moving on a Dated-related basis and a June 9-11 loader on a delivered basis to a northwest European refinery.
Two cargoes turning wet on Friday were clocked to Phibro and Cargill, two were kept by British Petroleum while the fifth was kept by Shell, traders said.
Brent cargoes are traded on a paper, or forward market until the 1700 London time deadline on the nearest trading day 15 days before their assigned loading date.
A trading company is clocked when it is left with a paper cargo which has turned physical after that deadline and therefore cannot be passed on as part of pre-sold paper cargo deals.
